    const UCRETSIZ: [&str; 6] = [
        "business.site", "wixsite.com", "blogspot.", "wordpress.com", "weebly.com", "webnode.",
    ];
    if SOSYAL.iter().any(|alan| kucuk.contains(alan)) {
        return Some(SiteDurumu::Sosyal);
    }
    if UCRETSIZ.iter().any(|alan| kucuk.contains(alan)) {
        return Some(SiteDurumu::Ucretsiz);
    }
    None
}

fn url_alan_adi(url: &str) -> String {
    let temiz = url.trim();
    let govde = temiz.split_once("://").map(|(_, kalan)| kalan).unwrap_or(temiz);
    let alan = govde

        .trim_end_matches('.')
        .to_ascii_lowercase()
}

    if let Some(alan_id) = alan_id {

                           // dolu bir ilçede 20'lik genel sınıra takılıp sessizce kesilirdi.
    const SOSYAL_DESEN: &str = "instagram|facebook|fb\\.com|linktr|tiktok|wa\\.me|twitter|x\\.com";
    const UCRETSIZ_DESEN: &str = "business\\.site|wixsite|blogspot|wordpress\\.com|weebly|webnode";
    let siteli_kota = SONUC_SINIRI - NIYETLI_KOTA;
    govde.push_str("(\n");
    for (anahtar, desen) in kurallar {
        govde.push_str(&format!(
            "  nwr[\"{anahtar}\"~\"{desen}\"][!\"website\"][!\"contact:website\"][!\"url\"][!\"contact:url\"]{hedef};\n"
        ));
    }
    govde.push_str(")->.sitesiz;\n(\n");
    for (anahtar, desen) in kurallar {
        for etiket in ["website", "contact:website"] {
            govde.push_str(&format!(
                "  nwr[\"{anahtar}\"~\"{desen}\"][\"{etiket}\"~\"{SOSYAL_DESEN}\",i]{hedef};\n"
            ));
            govde.push_str(&format!(
                "  nwr[\"{anahtar}\"~\"{desen}\"][\"{etiket}\"~\"{UCRETSIZ_DESEN}\",i]{hedef};\n"
            ));
        }
    }
    // meta: kaydın son düzenleme tarihi (tazelik) için gerekir.
    govde.push_str(&format!(
        ")->.niyetli;\n.sitesiz out meta center tags {siteli_kota};\n.niyetli out meta center tags {NIYETLI_KOTA};"
    ));
    format!("[out:json][timeout:60];\n{govde}")
}

## 1. The core mechanic everyone shares

Almost every tool in this list is a **Google Maps/Places scraper at heart**, and the "no website" test is simply: *is the `website` field on the Google Business Profile (GBP) empty?*

The important nuance — documented explicitly by Apify's no-website Actor and SiteBeacon — is that a blank website field is **"no page listed on Google," not "no web presence."** Two consequences the pros all deal with:
- **A Facebook/Instagram page in the website field counts as "has a website"** on a raw Maps field check. Businesses whose only web presence is a FB/IG page, a Booksy/Square booking link, or Google's own auto-generated profile page still need a real site.
- Conversely, some businesses *have* a site that just isn't listed on their GBP, so a blank field produces false positives.

- https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper
- https://sitebeacon.ai/faq

## 2. D7 Lead Finder

**Sources:** D7's site lists no API/portal origin. It returns business name, **website link**, email(s), postal address parts, and social handles (Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter), plus **review scores from Yelp, Facebook and Google** — meaning it is at minimum aggregating Maps + Yelp + Facebook, not Maps alone. D7 claims a database of 65M+ leads and up to 1,200 leads per search, in ~3 minutes. (D7 itself doesn't disclose its source list publicly; LeadSwift's comparison notes D7's helpdesk claims "150+ sources," which the author doubts.) https://d7leadfinder.com/ · https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder

**No-website detection:** D7 **exports a website column but does not offer an explicit "no website" filter** — the LeadSwift comparison states plainly that D7 "only allows you to sort columns in ascending/descending order," i.e. no filters for "no website," low ratings, missing socials, or "not running ads." So the practical workflow on D7 is: export → sort by website column → eyeball or filter blanks in Sheets. D7 gives no clarity on whether FB pages are normalized out of the website field; assume it just reports whatever Maps has.

**Lead-quality/intent signals D7 does provide** (this is its differentiator for web-design sales): Facebook Pixel / Google remarketing tag present, "actively running paid ads on Facebook/Messenger/Instagram or Yelp," mobile-friendly test, WordPress/Analytics/Schema detection, email provider detection (Google Apps/Outlook/Zoho), Instagram follower/like counts, and per-source review scores. That set is aimed at *"they have a site but it's bad or they're spending money"* rather than *"they have nothing."* https://d7leadfinder.com/

**Pipeline:** CSV/Excel/PDF/print export; free tier is live-only and **not exportable**. No CRM statuses, no contacted tracking, no suppression list — those simply don't exist in the product. (By contrast LeadSwift explicitly adds notes, pipeline status, and HTML/source-code search that D7 lacks.) https://d7leadfinder.com/ · https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder

**Pricing:** tiered monthly by *leads per report* and *searches per day*; free tier = 5 searches/day with non-exportable results (per homepage). Third-party trackers put entry plans around **$16.90/mo**, mid ~$26.90–$44.90, bulk/pro ~$77.90+, with other sources citing "$44.99/mo start" and credits/"100 credits free" — pricing is inconsistent across reviews, so treat numbers as indicative and check the choose-plan page. https://d7leadfinder.com/auth/choose-plan/ · https://tomba.io/blog/d7-lead-finder-pricing-reviews-pros-and-cons · https://fullenrich.com/content/d7-lead-finder-pricing

**Complaints:** unverified/generic emails (`info@`, `contact@`), stale listings, **duplicates and closed businesses in exports**, thin enrichment, weak support; nearly every reviewer describes a required "scrape → dedupe → verify" second step. https://tomba.io/blog/d7-lead-finder-pricing-reviews-pros-and-cons

## 3. Outscraper

**Sources:** Google Maps Scraper (their flagship), plus Google Search/Reviews/Images/News/Shopping, and an **Emails & Contacts Scraper** that crawls each business's website for emails, phones and social profiles. Not Yelp/Facebook-native — those come in only as scrape targets or as social links harvested from the business's own site. https://outscraper.com/pricing/ · https://outscraper.com/outscraper-google-maps-lead-generation/ equivalent page cited below

**No-website detection:** Outscraper's own lead-gen guide tells you to "**filter by minimum star rating, minimum review count, or whether a website URL is present**" in the advanced parameters panel *before* export. Their agencies playbook uses exactly "No website field in export" as the key filter signal for web-design agencies. Their "local businesses without websites" article is the clearest articulation of the rule: **"A stronger signal is an active business with reviews, a phone number, a clear category, and no website field"** — and explicitly warns not to treat a blank field alone as an opportunity. https://outscraper.com/outscraper-google-maps-generate-quality-leads/ · https://outscraper.com/local-businesses-without-websites/

**Does FB/IG count as a website?** Outscraper treats social-only as a *separate* condition rather than folding it into "has website": their industry list calls salons, studios, restaurants and event services out for "**social-only presence, booking link**" and "third-party menu links / delivery app dependence." Their advice is to filter on missing website field and *then* manually/semi-automatically check whether social or booking pages are the real web presence. There is no native "exclude facebook.com from the website field" toggle documented. https://outscraper.com/local-businesses-without-websites/

**Quality/intent signals:** rating (with the explicit rule "3.8/under = reputation problem," 4.0+ = premium B2B), review count, category, address, hours, review text, **business status (closed listings should be removed)**. They also publish a "website gap" industry scorecard — home services, contractors, landscaping, auto repair, cleaning, salons/barbers, restaurants, childcare, pet services, fitness, events, local professional services — which is genuinely useful for picking niches. Citing Clutch, ~17% of small businesses still have no website. https://outscraper.com/local-businesses-without-websites/ · https://outscraper.com/outscraper-google-maps-generate-quality-leads/

**Pipeline:** cloud tasks with history/re-download, duplicate-removal option when running multiple queries (e.g. "lawyers in NY" vs "attorneys in NY"), up to 500 results/query default, CSV/Excel/JSON/Parquet export, REST API, scheduled/enrichment pipelines. No CRM/contacted-tracking layer — that's left to their integrations. https://blackbearmedia.io/outscraper-review/ · https://outscraper.com/pricing/

**Pricing:** pure pay-as-you-go, no subscription. Google Maps Scraper: **free for first 500 businesses**, then **$3/1,000 records** up to 100k, then **$1/1,000**. Reviews scraper the same. Emails & Contacts Scraper: 500 free domains, then $3/1,000; email verifier $3/1,000 after 25 free; phone lookup $5/1,000. Credits never expire; tiers reset every 30 days. https://outscraper.com/pricing/

**Complaints:** the recurring one is exactly the false-positive problem — a reviewer notes that of "300 businesses in SF with no website," many still have a Google listing and an existing (unlisted) site; also requires self-directed filtering afterwards, and pay-per-record costs scale quickly for large territory runs. https://blackbearmedia.io/outscraper-review/

## 4. LeadSwift

**Sources:** aggregates from **Google Maps, Yelp, Facebook, YellowPages and other directories**, plus per-business website crawling, plus review/rating data from Google, Facebook, Bing, Yelp, TripAdvisor, YellowPages. https://localprospects.ai/reviews/leadswift · https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder

**No-website detection:** has a **true built-in filter layer over any data point** — "businesses that don't have a website," ratings below a threshold *or missing entirely*, missing social profiles, not running ads, plus **HTML/source-code search** ("Powered By [competitor]") for tech-stack-based targeting. This is the single biggest structural difference from D7 (sort-only) and why agencies pick it. It does **not** document treating FB/IG as a website explicitly; because it ingests Facebook as a source, the website field can include social URLs, and the practical approach is to filter for missing website *and* cross-check social fields. It also uniquely reports **whether the Google listing is "claimed"**, whether the website is working/broken, and business status ("temporarily closed"). https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder

**Quality signals:** Google/Yelp/Facebook ratings and review counts, claimed/unclaimed GBP, website working/broken, mobile compatibility, page speed, SEO deficiencies, ad-running status, email provider, staff names/emails, and automated **website audit reports** that can be pasted into outreach — the classic web-design pitch asset. https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder

**Pipeline:** the most complete of the four SMB tools — built-in CRM-ish lead notes + pipeline status, unlimited contacts/exports/data points, unlimited senders, follow-ups with open-triggers, shared inbox, third-party email verification (ZeroBounce, NeverBounce, Hunter, MailTester) reused across users, **notifications when another user re-runs your saved search and new leads appear** (a de-facto suppression/"already seen" mechanism), plus API and Zapier/n8n/GoHighLevel. https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder · https://localprospects.ai/reviews/leadswift

**Pricing:** Starter **$24.99/mo (1 search/day)**, Professional **$49.99 (5/day)**, Agency **$99.99 (20/day)**; annual $19.99/$39.99/$79.99. **7-day free trial, no credit card.** All plans include unlimited leads, exports, contacts, outreach — only search count varies; annual plans pausable up to 3 months. https://leadswift.com/pricing · https://localprospects.ai/reviews/leadswift

**Complaints:** generic `info@` emails, **missing or out-of-date owner names**, uneven/stale lists ("same industry same city, different lead counts"), only 1 search/day on Starter with **unused searches expiring**, dated UI, hard SMTP setup, no mobile/landline line-type detection; reviewers note the ~4.9 Trustpilot score comes largely from invited reviews, and G2 profile isn't claimed. https://localprospects.ai/reviews/leadswift

## 5. Apify (Google Maps Scraper + no-website Actors)

**Sources:** Google Maps directly (bypassing the Places API and Google's 120-results-per-area display cap), with optional add-ons for website contact scraping, German/Austrian/Swiss Impressum extraction, LinkedIn-style lead enrichment, and social-profile enrichment (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Twitter). https://apify.com/compass/crawler-google-places

**No-website detection:** two models.
- **The generic Compass scraper** returns `website` (empty when none), `claimThisBusiness`, `permanentlyClosed`, `temporarilyClosed`, `reviewsCount`, `totalScore`, `categories`, `phone` — you filter downstream. Note the presence of a **`claimThisBusiness` boolean**, which is the direct unclaimed-listing signal. https://apify.com/compass/crawler-google-places
- **Purpose-built "No-Website Leads" Actors** implement the classification properly, and this is the best-documented answer to your FB question: it emits a `presence` field of `none` / `social_only` / `booking_only` / `broken_website` / `has_website`, and **deliberately never writes a Facebook/Booksy/GBP-placeholder link into `websiteUrl`** — social pages go to `weakPresenceUrl`, dead sites to `brokenWebsiteUrl`. It also does an optional live `checkWebsiteStatus` and treats bot-walled sites as live (avoids false "broken" leads), scores leads 0–100 from presence + phone + reviews + rating, and **keeps no-rating/no-review/no-category businesses rather than dropping them** (arguing a no-website, no-review listing is often the strongest lead). Example output row: presence, leadScore 95, phone, 4.4 rating, 1,400 reviews. https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper

**Quality filters available:** `minRating`, `minReviews`, `requirePhone`, `categoryContains`, `maxLeadsPerQuery`, `checkWebsiteStatus`, `onlyNew`, `excludePlaceIds`, `baselineDatasetId`. Category matching is flagged as risky in both directions (false positives from search terms, false negatives because Google has thousands of near-synonym categories — e.g. "Divorce lawyer/service/attorney" are three distinct categories). https://apify.com/compass/crawler-google-places · https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper

**Pipeline:** datasets with CSV/JSON/Excel/XML/HTML export, named views ("No-website leads view"), **scheduling via saved Tasks**, **repeat-run deduplication by `placeId`** (`onlyNew` / baseline datset import), **suppression via `excludePlaceIds`**, webhooks, MCP server, Make/Zapier/Sheets. No CRM statuses — you pipe to your own. https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper

**Pricing:** platform is **Free $0 (with $5 monthly usage credit, no card)** / Starter $19 / Scale $199 / Business $999 + pay-as-you-go; Actors are "pay per event" or "pay per usage." Compass Maps Scraper: **from $1.50 per 1,000 scraped places** (third-party analyses put real cost at ~$4–7/1,000 once enrichment and proxies are added). The no-website Actor is **$10 per 1,000 matching leads**, charged only on matches, not on scans. https://apify.com/pricing · https://apify.com/compass/crawler-google-places · https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper

**Complaints/limits:** raw scrapers need you to build the taxonomy yourself; you pay for scanning in the generic model; category filters cause silent misses; Actor quality varies wildly across community publishers (the no-website Actor itself has a 2.0 rating on 3 reviews) and Apify's reddit-cost comparisons show it getting expensive at 10k–20k/month versus flat-rate competitors. https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper

## 6. SerpApi (Google Maps API)

**Sources:** Google Maps only — search results, place results, reviews, photos. No Yelp/OSM/Facebook. https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api

**No-website detection:** there is **no "no website" parameter**. You request places, then check whether `website` is present in `place_results`. What SerpApi *does* expose that the scrapers mostly don't:
- **`unclaimed_listing: true`** — "Some business places are not yet claimed," explicitly documented. (Plus `claimed`/ownership-style fields.) https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api
- `business_status` style closed flags, `hours_last_updated` ("Confirmed by this business 4 weeks ago") — a real dormancy signal, since an unconfirmed listing is likely neglected.
- `min_rating` / `max_rating` / `min_price` / `max_price` relevance filters, `open_state`, `open_on_day`, `open_at_hour`.

**Critical limitation for this use case:** SerpApi's filters are *relevance* filters, not hard filters — "Places without a rating or with a rating below the specified value **can still be returned**, but with reduced relevance." Same applies to rating filters; you must filter in code. Pagination caps at ~100 offset. https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api

**Pipeline:** JSON (or HTML, or Markdown for LLMs), `json_restrictor` for payload trimming, `no_cache` (cached=free), `async` + Search Archive, ZeroTrace (Enterprise). **No CRM, no dedup, no suppression list, no CSV** — it's an API primitive, so every pipeline feature is yours to build. https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api

**Pricing:** credit-based monthly search plans (not verified in detail from the pages I read — see caveat). Free tier is small (~100 searches/mo historically); cached repeat queries are free and don't burn quota.

**Complaints/limits:** you pay per search regardless of whether results are useful; relevance-based rather than exact filtering; results "not guaranteed to be within the geographic location provided in `ll`" — a documented accuracy caveat that matters when you're promising a client "every plumber in this ZIP code." https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api

## 7. PhantomBuster

**Sources:** Google Maps via a "Google Maps Search Export" Phantom (business, contact, social, website data per location) plus a companion Flow ("Google Maps Search to Contact Data") that extracts emails, phone numbers and social handles. Broader platform covers LinkedIn/Sales Nav etc. **Note: phantom's own pages returned no extractable text** (JS-only rendering), so PhantomBuster specifics below are from their support docs and the tutorial ecosystem, not the product page. https://phantombuster.com/automations/google-maps/23412/google-maps-search-export · https://support.phantombuster.com/hc/en-us/articles/4494623647250-What-Each-PhantomBuster-Plan-Includes-Features-Limits-and-Pricing

**No-website detection:** **no native "no website" filter** — it exports the Maps search results as-is; the widely-shared tutorial workflow ("How to Find Local Businesses With NO Website — 29 Leads in Under 30 Minutes" using Google Maps + PhantomBuster) is a **Google Sheet/CSV step: export → filter the website column for blanks**. No documented normalization of Facebook pages. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VyZ_1G_DvvM

**Pipeline:** unlimited CSV/JSON exports on paid plans (**10-row cap on free/trial**), API access, Workflows to chain Phantoms (e.g. Maps → contact scraping), scheduling, up to 100 workspace members. No CRM statuses/suppression lists — that's downstream. https://support.phantombuster.com/hc/en-us/articles/4494623647250-What-Each-PhantomBuster-Plan-Includes-Features-Limits-and-Pricing

## 8. How local marketing agencies actually run the workflow

Synthesizing the vendor playbooks and the purpose-built agency tools, the professional pipeline looks like this:

1. **Territory + niche grid.** Category + city/ZIP, deliberately *narrow* ("HVAC contractor," not "contractor"), and multiple near-synonym categories because Google's taxonomy is inconsistent. Agencies run city-by-city rather than "all of California" because coverage per query is capped. https://outscraper.com/outscraper-google-maps-generate-quality-leads/ · https://apify.com/compass/crawler-google-places
2. **Pull, then filter on a composite, not a single field.** The consensus formula from Outscraper: *active business + clear category + phone number + reviews + missing website field*. Explicitly: a blank website with no reviews, no phone and vague details is **not** a lead. https://outscraper.com/local-businesses-without-websites/
3. **Separate "no site at all" from "weak presence."** Third-party badge schemes show the actual vocabulary: **"No Site Listed"** (GBP has no website) → upgraded to **"No Website ✓"** only after independently searching directories, Facebook and Instagram and coming up empty; **"Third Party"** (Wix, Squarespace, Facebook page, Yelp, ordering page as the sole presence); **"Has Website"** (lower design fit, still SEO/GBP fit). A composite **lead score 1–100** is used, where **no website is the single largest positive weight (+35)**, with low rating and incomplete GBP also raising it and having a real site lowering it. https://sitebeacon.ai/faq
4. **Score/qualify the GBP itself.** Missing hours, no photos, thin description, missing phone or website link, few reviews = "GBP lead" for local SEO. `unclaimed_listing` (SerpApi) and `claimThisBusiness` (Apify) are the machine-readable versions of this. https://sitebeacon.ai/faq · https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api
5. **Attach evidence to the pitch.** The recurring conversion asset is a **generated website audit / scorecard** (mobile, load time, SEO gaps, malware, indexing) or a GBP-completeness report, sent as a hosted link — LeadSwift and SiteBeacon both productize this. https://leadswift.com/comparison/d7-lead-finder · https://sitebeacon.ai/faq
6. **Track status and never re-contact.** Real agency pipelines need *Saved leads → status/notes → queued follow-ups → do-not-contact list*. Only the purpose-built tools have this natively; scrapers require CRM + CSV round-trips. https://sitebeacon.ai/faq
7. **Re-run with dedup.** Professional-grade features to look for: `placeId`-based "only new since last run," suppression via exclude-lists, and annual plans that let you pause out of season. https://apify.com/webdata_labs/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper · https://leadswift.com/pricing
8. **Compliance guardrail.** Google only permits storing business listing data for ~30 days, which is why at least one tool expires raw search results after 30 days and requires you to explicitly save leads you intend to keep. https://sitebeacon.ai/faq

## Bottom line

Sending unsolicited WhatsApp sales messages to Turkish businesses as a first contact is **legally grey-leaning-prohibited under KVKK** and **flatly prohibited by WhatsApp's own policy** (which requires opt-in from every recipient, including businesses). The İYS/e-commerce rules, by contrast, do *not* require prior consent for messages to *tacir/esnaf* recipients — that exemption, however, only removes the İYS problem, not the KVKK or Meta problem.

---

## 1. KVKK — does a sole proprietor's phone number count as personal data?

**Yes.** KVKK's definition is tied to *real persons*:

- Art. 3(d): "Kişisel veri: Kimliği belirli veya belirlenebilir **gerçek kişiye** ilişkin her türlü bilgiyi"; Art. 3(ç): "İlgili kişi: kişisel verisi işlenen **gerçek kişi**" ([6698 consolidated text](https://www.lexpera.com.tr/mevzuat/kanunlar/kisisel-verilerin-korunmasi-kanunu-6698)).
- Art. 2(1) limits scope to real persons whose data is processed; legal entities (tüzel kişiler) themselves fall outside the Act.

Practical consequence: a *limited company's* corporate switchboard is arguably not personal data, but a **sole proprietor (şahıs işletmesi / esnaf) is a real person**, so his mobile number, name, and T.C. kimlik no are personal data. The same is true for a named contact person (owner, manager, "yetkili") at any company — a mobile number tied to a natural person remains personal data even if used for business.

**Legal basis for processing:** KVKK Art. 5(1) — no processing without explicit consent unless one of the Art. 5(2) grounds applies (statute, contract performance, legal obligation, made public by the data subject, establishment of a right, legitimate interest). Art. 5(2)(f) legitimate interest is the only realistic candidate for cold B2B outreach, and it must be balanced case-by-case.

**Enforcement reality (important):** the Kurul's practice has been hostile to unsolicited marketing. Its 16.10.2018 / 2018/119 ilke kararı ordered data controllers to **stop immediately** sending advertising SMS/calls/e-mails to numbers without consent or another Art. 5 ground, and recent decisions fine controllers for unconsented commercial e-mails/SMS. Critically, the Kurul has held that data **scraped from search engines / publicly listed business e-mails cannot rely on "alenileştirme"** (Art. 5(2)(d)) — being public for one purpose does not license marketing use. It also stresses that the **aydınlatma yükümlülüğü (Art. 10)** applies even where consent is not needed. ([Gün + Partners analysis of KVKK Kurul decisions on commercial electronic messages](https://gun.av.tr/tr/goruslerimiz/guncel-yazilar/ticari-elektronik-ileti-gonderimi-hakkinda-kisisel-verileri-koruma-kurulu-kararlari))

**Sanctions:** KVKK Art. 18 administrative fines (Art. 12 data-security failures: 15,000–1,000,000 TL, re-valued annually), plus Art. 17 references TCK 135–140 criminal provisions for unlawful recording of personal data. Art. 10/12 fines are the realistic exposure for unconsented outreach at volume.

**What this means for you:** harvesting numbers from Google Maps/websites and blasting them is the highest-risk pattern. A sole trader's mobile is personal data, there is no consent, and the "alenileştirme" defence has already been rejected by the Kurul.

---

## 2. Ticari Elektronik İleti Yönetmeliği / İYS — is prior consent required for businesses?

**No, not for tacir/esnaf recipients — but İYS registration and a "ret hakkı" check are still mandatory.**

Primary text: [Ticari İletişim ve Ticari Elektronik İletiler Hakkında Yönetmelik (consolidated, RG 15.07.2015/29417, last amended RG 04.01.2020/30998)](https://www.lexpera.com.tr/mevzuat/yonetmelikler/ticari-iletisim-ve-ticari-elektronik-iletiler-hakkinda-yonetmelik). Key provisions:

- **Art. 4(1)(a) "Alıcı"** = "Tüketiciyi **ya da meslekî veya diğer amaçlarla hareket eden gerçek veya tüzel kişiyi**" — so B2B recipients are within scope.
- **Art. 4(1)(o) "Ticari elektronik ileti"** = messages "**Telefon**, çağrı merkezleri, faks, otomatik arama makineleri, akıllı ses kaydedici sistemler, elektronik posta, kısa mesaj hizmeti **gibi vasıtalar** kullanılarak elektronik ortamda gerçekleştirilen ve ticari amaçlarla gönderilen veri, ses ve görüntü içerikli iletiler." WhatsApp messages fit the "telefon… gibi vasıtalar" (non-exhaustive "such as") formula and are sent over an electronic communications network — they are commercial electronic messages. (Ticaret Bakanlığı uses the same definition: [ticaret.gov.tr e-ticaret SSS](https://ticaret.gov.tr/ic-ticaret/sikca-sorulan-sorular/elektronik-ticaret).)
- **Art. 5(1)–(3):** prior consent required, sender must register in İYS, and "İYS üzerinde onayı bulunmayan alıcılara ticari elektronik ileti gönderilemez."
- **Art. 6(3) — the B2B carve-out:** "**Tacir veya esnaf olan alıcıların** elektronik iletişim adreslerine gönderilen ticari elektronik iletiler için **önceden onay alınması zorunlu değildir.** Ancak tacir ve esnafların 9 uncu maddede yer alan reddetme hakkını kullanması halinde onayları alınmadan ticari elektronik ileti gönderilemez."
- **Art. 6(6) — the obligation that survives B2B:** "…ileti gönderilmesinden önce tacir veya esnaf olan alıcıların elektronik iletişim adresleri hizmet sağlayıcı tarafından **İYS'ye kaydedilir ve İYS üzerinden alıcıların ret hakkını kullanıp kullanmadığı kontrol edilir.**"
- **Art. 8(2)–(3) — mandatory content:** MERSİS no + ticaret unvanı for tacir; ad-soyad + T.C./vergi kimlik no for esnaf; at least one reachable contact detail; a "tanıtım/kampanya" identifier if the nature isn't obvious.
- **Art. 9(3)–(4):** every message must offer a **free opt-out through the same channel** it was sent on ("Ticari elektronik ileti hangi iletişim kanalıyla gönderildiyse ret bildirimi de kolay ve ücretsiz bir şekilde olmak üzere aynı iletişim kanalıyla sağlanır").
- **Art. 10:** stop sending within **3 business days** of an opt-out; Art. 7(12) & 13(2): consent records must be logged in İYS within 3 business days and kept 3 years; the burden of proof is on the sender.
- **Art. 12:** personal data can only be shared/processed for other purposes with prior consent of the data subject — the bridge to KVKK.
- **Art. 14:** complaints go to İYS / e-Devlet / Ticaret İl Müdürlüğü within 3 months; a recipient (or their business) may complain.

**Statutory basis:** 6563 sayılı Kanun Art. 6(2): "Esnaf ve tacirlere önceden onay alınmaksızın ticari elektronik iletiler gönderilebilir"; Art. 12(2): sending to **multiple persons at once** in breach of Art. 6(1) raises the fine "**on katına kadar**" ([6563 RG text](https://www.lexpera.com.tr/resmi-gazete/metin/elektronik-ticaretin-duzenlenmesi-hakkinda-kanun-29166-6563)). Fines are re-valued yearly by Tebliğ ([2025 Tebliğ summary](https://www.zumbul.av.tr/tr/duyurular/elektronik-ticaretin-duzenlenmesi-hakk-nda-kanunun-2025-yili-icin-idari-para-cezalari)).

**Caveats you must not miss:**
1. The B2B exemption applies to **tacir/esnaf**, i.e. registered businesses. If the contact is a *consumer* or an unregistered individual (e.g., a freelancer not registered as esnaf), full prior consent is required.
2. İYS currently manages consents under the Reg onay/ret framework built around e-mail and SMS/number-based channels; **there is no operational "WhatsApp" approval channel** in İYS. In practice, agencies either (a) treat a WhatsApp number as a "telefon numarası" for İYS ret-control purposes, or (b) rely on Art. 6(3) but keep an internal do-not-contact list — and document the ret-control step, because Art. 13 puts the burden of proof on you. (I could not fetch the İYS FAQ body — iys.org.tr renders client-side and returned only the page title — so I could not verify any İYS-specific statement about WhatsApp channels; treat this point as practice, not verified İYS text.)
3. **Exemption from İYS ≠ exemption from KVKK.** Art. 6(3) removes the *consent* requirement under e-commerce law; it does not create an Art. 5 KVKK ground, and the Kurul has repeatedly treated unconsented marketing contact as unlawful processing. This is the single most common misconception.

## 3. WhatsApp / Meta policy — unsolicited messaging, and what happens to your number

**Opt-in is mandatory, for every recipient, including businesses.** The [WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy (last updated 23.09.2026)](https://whatsappbusiness.com/policy/) states:

> "You may only contact people on WhatsApp if: (a) they have given you their mobile phone number or username; and (b) you have received **opt-in permission** from the recipient confirming that they wish to receive subsequent messages or calls from you. **You are solely responsible for determining the method of opt-in**, that you have obtained opt-in in a manner that complies with laws applicable to your communications…"

And on enforcement: "We may limit or remove your access… if you receive **significant amounts of negative feedback**… Our systems may limit the amount of messages a business can send… based on this user feedback." Plus: "If you use or operate a service which utilizes WhatsApp in violation… such as **messaging people at scale in an unauthorized manner**, we have the right to limit or remove your access."

**Platform (Cloud API) specifics** ([same policy, §2](https://whatsappbusiness.com/policy/)): you may only **initiate** with an approved **Message Template**; free-form replies only inside the **24-hour customer service window**; automation allowed only with a clear human escalation path. So "cold" first contact via the API is structurally impossible without violating policy — the template gate + opt-in requirement means cold lists cannot be messaged compliantly.

**Enforcement ladder** (official: [WhatsApp Business Platform policy and spam enforcement](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/policy-enforcement)) — there is **no published "X messages per day" ban threshold**; enforcement is feedback-driven and escalates:
1. Warning naming the violated policy;
2. **1- or 3-day block** on sending marketing/utility/authentication templates + on adding numbers;
3. **5-, 7-, or 30-day block** on sending *any* messages + adding numbers;
4. **Account lock** — indefinite block, only removable via appeal;
5. **Permanent disablement** from the Business Platform; for severe violations (scams, etc.) immediate offboarding.
Also: "We might also limit or offboard your business… if your account receives excessive negative feedback from users," and "Not all spam violations might be appealed."

**Messaging limits** ([official Messaging Limits doc](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messaging-limits)): as of the current docs, limits are **per business portfolio, shared across all numbers** in it (not per number), and define the max number of **unique** users you can message **outside a customer-service window** in a rolling 24h: new portfolios start at **250**, then 2,000 → 10,000 → 100,000 → unlimited via business verification / automatic scaling (requires sending 2,000 high-quality template messages in 30 days, then using ≥50% of the limit in 7 days with high quality). Note this only caps *template* outbound for opted-in users — it is not a licence to cold-message.

**Practical implication:** a brand-new number that sends dozens of unsolicited first-touch messages will typically see high block/report rates almost immediately, which is exactly the signal that triggers the 1/3/5/7/30-day ladder — long before any volume cap.

---

## 4. Practical safe limits and best practices agencies actually use

Caveat first: **these are practitioner heuristics, not published Meta or Turkish rules**. Meta publishes no safe daily cap for unsolicited sends precisely because unsolicited sends are disallowed.

From published agency guidance ([SBL.so WhatsApp B2B cold outreach guide](https://sbl.so/whatsapp/whatsapp-cold-outreach-b2b-guide/)) — note this is a vendor selling non-official automation, so treat its numbers as anecdotal:

- **New numbers:** warm up at **10–20 messages/day**, scaling over **2–3 weeks**; unofficial/self-API automation vendors cite **25–50 messages/day per number** as their ceiling.
- **Block rate:** keep **under ~2%**; sustained breaches degrade quality and lead to restriction.
- **Opt-out line in every message** ("If WhatsApp isn't the right channel, tell me and I'll email instead") — this explicitly protects account quality.
- **One follow-up maximum** on WhatsApp (vs 4–5 in e-mail); a third message feels like harassment and gets you blocked.
- **Position WhatsApp as the 3rd/4th touch** in a multi-channel sequence (LinkedIn → e-mail → WhatsApp), referencing the earlier touch in line 1, and always say **how you got their number**.
- Benchmarks they report: cold first-touch WhatsApp ~3–5% reply; semi-warm 8–15%; opted-in (CTWA ads/form fills) 20–40%+.
- Keep **consent/source logs with timestamps**; use a **dedicated business number**, never a personal one.

**wa.me / click-to-chat vs automation — the honest trade-off:**
- `wa.me` / click-to-chat **with a human typing each message** is not "automation" and does not breach the API template rules — but it is still WhatsApp *messaging* and therefore still subject to the Messaging Policy's opt-in requirement and to KVKK. It reduces the *platform* risk signal (fewer identical templates, natural pacing, real replies) but does **not** make cold outreach compliant with Turkish law.
- Third-party "WhatsApp self-API" / browser-automation senders (unofficial, QR-code based) are the pattern Meta explicitly targets as "messaging people at scale in an unauthorized manner" — highest ban risk, and they give you no compliance shield at all.

---

## Recommended compliant-ish playbook for your use case

1. **Don't cold-DM sole proprietors' mobiles.** Get the number via a channel where the contact *gave* it for this purpose (web form with a marketing checkbox, a WhatsApp click-to-chat ad, a referral, a trade-show badge scan, an inbound message) — that single change fixes both KVKK Art. 5 and Meta's opt-in requirement.
2. **If you must do semi-cold B2B:** target only registered tacir/esnaf, send **1:1, hand-typed** from a warmed business number, ≤10–20/day at the start, identify your firm (MERSİS/unvan or ad-soyad + vergi no), state how you got the number, include a free same-channel opt-out ("reddetmek için 'RET' yazın"), honour it within 3 business days, and **keep a log of date, number, source, and opt-out** — Art. 13 puts the burden of proof on you and you must retain records 3 years.
3. **Register in İYS** if you send anything at volume (you're a "hizmet sağlayıcı"), and depending on your lawyer's read, upload the business numbers as "elektronik iletişim adresi" for ret-control under Art. 6(6).
4. **Publish a KVKK aydınlatma metni** covering B2B prospect data, name an Art. 5(2)(f) legitimate-interest basis explicitly, and register with VERBİS if you cross the Kurul's thresholds.
5. **Never** buy scraped number lists, never use unofficial bulk senders, and never put the same template into a broadcast to hundreds of numbers.

**What I could not verify:** mevzuat.gov.tr and several kvkk.gov.tr PDFs timed out / returned HTTP 500 through the tool, so I relied on Lexpera's consolidated texts of the Reg and of 6563 (which link to RG 05.11.2014/29166 and RG 15.07.2015/29417) and on the Ticaret Bakanlığı's own FAQ; iys.org.tr renders client-side and only returned its page title, so İYS's own handling of WhatsApp numbers is unverified. The 2025 fine amounts appear only in a secondary summary — quote the Tebliğ itself before relying on figures.

    }
}

//! Dosya biçimi JSON'dur (`musteri_kayitlari.json`); sürüm alanı ileride
//! şema değişirse taşıma için tutulur.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs;

/// Varsayılan defter dosyası (çalışma dizininde, .gitignore'da).
pub const DEFTER_DOSYASI: &str = "musteri_kayitlari.json";
const SURUM: u32 = 1;

/// Bir işletmeyle ilişkinin bulunduğu aşama.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum Durum {
    /// Henüz temas kurulmadı.
    #[default]
    Yeni,
    /// Demo/mesaj hazırlandı ama gönderilmedi.
    MesajHazir,
    /// Mesaj gönderildi, yanıt bekleniyor.
    Gonderildi,
    /// İşletme ilgilendi.
    Ilgilendi,
    /// İşletme istemedi: kara liste, bir daha temas kurulmaz.
    Reddetti,
}

impl Durum {
    pub fn etiket(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Durum::Yeni => "yeni",
            Durum::MesajHazir => "mesaj hazır",
            Durum::Gonderildi => "gönderildi",
            Durum::Ilgilendi => "ilgileniyor",
            Durum::Reddetti => "kara listede",
        }
    }

    /// Sıralama ağırlığı: taze fırsatlar önce, temas edilmişler sonra.
    pub fn sira(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Durum::Yeni => 0,
            Durum::MesajHazir => 1,
            Durum::Ilgilendi => 2,
            Durum::Gonderildi => 3,
            Durum::Reddetti => 4,
        }
    }

    /// Kara listedeki işletmeye mesaj hazırlanmaz.
    pub fn kara_listede(self) -> bool {
        self == Durum::Reddetti
    }

    /// CSV'ye yazılan kararlı ad (Türkçe karakter yok, Excel'de bozulmasın).
    pub fn kod(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Durum::Yeni => "yeni",
            Durum::MesajHazir => "mesaj_hazir",
            Durum::Gonderildi => "gonderildi",
            Durum::Ilgilendi => "ilgilendi",
            Durum::Reddetti => "reddetti",
        }
    }
}

/// Defterdeki tek müşteri kaydı.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Musteri {
    pub anahtar: String,
    pub ad: String,
    pub telefon: String,
    pub adres: String,
    pub kategori: String,
    pub kaynak: String,
    /// Web varlığı: "yok" / "sosyal" / "ucretsiz".
    pub site: String,
    pub site_linki: String,
    /// Satın alma potansiyeli puanı (0-100), son taramadaki değer.
    pub puan: u8,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub durum: Durum,
    pub ilk_gorulme: String,
    pub son_gorulme: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub son_temas: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub notlar: String,
}

/// Defterin özet sayaçları (arayüzde ve günlükte gösterilir).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Ozet {
    pub toplam: usize,
    pub yeni: usize,
    pub gonderilen: usize,
    pub ilgilenen: usize,
    pub kara_liste: usize,
}

#[derive(Default, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct Dosya {
    #[serde(default)]
    surum: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    musteriler: Vec<Musteri>,
}

/// Kalıcı defter: kayıtlar + anahtar→indeks eşlemesi.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Defter {
    dosya: Dosya,
    indeks: HashMap<String, usize>,
}

impl Defter {
    /// Dosyadan yükler; dosya yoksa veya bozuksa boş defter döner.
    pub fn yukle() -> Self {
        Self::yukle_yoldan(DEFTER_DOSYASI)
    }

    pub fn yukle_yoldan(yol: &str) -> Self {
        let metin = fs::read_to_string(yol).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut defter = Self::metinden(&metin);
        defter.dosya.surum = SURUM;
        defter
    }

    /// JSON metninden defter kurar (bozuk metin → boş defter).
    pub fn metinden(metin: &str) -> Self {
        let dosya: Dosya = serde_json::from_str(metin).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut defter = Self {
            dosya,
            indeks: HashMap::new(),
        };
        defter.indeks_yenile();
        defter
    }

    pub fn kaydet(&self) {
        if let Ok(metin) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&self.dosya) {
            let _ = fs::write(DEFTER_DOSYASI, metin);
        }
    }

    fn indeks_yenile(&mut self) {
        self.indeks.clear();
        for (sira, musteri) in self.dosya.musteriler.iter().enumerate() {
            self.indeks.insert(musteri.anahtar.clone(), sira);
        }
    }

    /// Tarama sonucunu deftere işler ve işletmenin güncel durumunu döndürür.
    /// Yeni kayıt eklenir, var olanın iletişim bilgileri ve puanı tazelenir;
    /// durum (gönderildi/reddetti...) korunur.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn isle(
        &mut self,
        anahtar: &str,
        ad: &str,
        telefon: &str,
        adres: &str,
        kategori: &str,
        kaynak: &str,
        site: &str,
        site_linki: &str,
        puan: u8,
        tarih: &str,
    ) -> Durum {
        if let Some(&sira) = self.indeks.get(anahtar) {
            let musteri = &mut self.dosya.musteriler[sira];
            musteri.ad = ad.to_string();
            musteri.telefon = telefon.to_string();
            musteri.adres = adres.to_string();
            musteri.kategori = kategori.to_string();
            musteri.kaynak = kaynak.to_string();
            musteri.site = site.to_string();
            musteri.site_linki = site_linki.to_string();
            musteri.puan = puan;
            musteri.son_gorulme = tarih.to_string();
            return musteri.durum;
        }
        let musteri = Musteri {
            anahtar: anahtar.to_string(),
            ad: ad.to_string(),
            telefon: telefon.to_string(),
            adres: adres.to_string(),
            kategori: kategori.to_string(),
            kaynak: kaynak.to_string(),
            site: site.to_string(),
            site_linki: site_linki.to_string(),
            puan,
            durum: Durum::Yeni,
            ilk_gorulme: tarih.to_string(),
            son_gorulme: tarih.to_string(),
            son_temas: None,
            notlar: String::new(),
        };
        self.indeks.insert(anahtar.to_string(), self.dosya.musteriler.len());
        self.dosya.musteriler.push(musteri);
        Durum::Yeni
    }

    /// İşletmenin durumunu değiştirir. İlk temas tarihi yalnızca bir kez yazılır.
    pub fn durum_ayarla(&mut self, anahtar: &str, durum: Durum, tarih: &str) {
        if let Some(&sira) = self.indeks.get(anahtar) {
            let musteri = &mut self.dosya.musteriler[sira];
            musteri.durum = durum;
            if musteri.son_temas.is_none() && durum != Durum::Yeni {
                musteri.son_temas = Some(tarih.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn durum(&self, anahtar: &str) -> Durum {
        self.indeks
            .get(anahtar)
            .map(|&sira| self.dosya.musteriler[sira].durum)
            .unwrap_or(Durum::Yeni)
    }

    pub fn kayit(&self, anahtar: &str) -> Option<&Musteri> {
        self.indeks
            .get(anahtar)
            .map(|&sira| &self.dosya.musteriler[sira])
    }

    pub fn kayitlar(&self) -> &[Musteri] {
        &self.dosya.musteriler
    }

    pub fn ozet(&self) -> Ozet {
        let mut ozet = Ozet {
            toplam: self.dosya.musteriler.len(),
            ..Ozet::default()
        };
        for musteri in &self.dosya.musteriler {
            match musteri.durum {
                Durum::Yeni => ozet.yeni += 1,
                Durum::Gonderildi | Durum::MesajHazir => ozet.gonderilen += 1,
                Durum::Ilgilendi => ozet.ilgilenen += 1,
                Durum::Reddetti => ozet.kara_liste += 1,
            }
        }
        ozet
    }

    /// Excel'in Türkçe yerel ayarında doğru açılan CSV (';' ayraçlı).
    pub fn csv(&self) -> String {
        let mut cikti = String::from(
            "ad;telefon;adres;kategori;site;site_linki;puan;durum;ilk_gorulme;son_gorulme;son_temas;kaynak\n",
        );
        for musteri in &self.dosya.musteriler {
            let alanlar = [
                musteri.ad.as_str(),
                musteri.telefon.as_str(),
                musteri.adres.as_str(),
                musteri.kategori.as_str(),
                musteri.site.as_str(),
                musteri.site_linki.as_str(),
                &musteri.puan.to_string(),
                musteri.durum.kod(),
                musteri.ilk_gorulme.as_str(),
                musteri.son_gorulme.as_str(),
                musteri.son_temas.as_deref().unwrap_or(""),
                musteri.kaynak.as_str(),
            ];
            let satir: Vec<String> = alanlar.iter().map(|alan| csv_alan(alan)).collect();
            cikti.push_str(&satir.join(";"));
            cikti.push('\n');
        }
        cikti
    }
}

/// CSV alanı: ayraç, tırnak veya satır sonu varsa tırnak içine alınır.
fn csv_alan(metin: &str) -> String {
    let kacis_gerekli = metin
        .chars()
        .any(|harf| matches!(harf, ';' | '"' | '\n' | '\r'));
    if kacis_gerekli {
        format!("\"{}\"", metin.replace('"', "\"\""))
    } else {
        metin.to_string()
    }
}

/// Kayıt anahtarı: işletmeyi taramalar arasında eşleştiren kararlı kimlik.
/// OSM kaydı için node/way kimliği, Google için place ID, yoksa ad+koordinat.
pub fn anahtar_uret(kaynak: &str, ad: &str, konum: Option<(f64, f64)>) -> String {
    if let Some(kalan) = kaynak.split("openstreetmap.org/").nth(1) {
        return format!("osm:{}", kalan.trim_end_matches('/'));
    }
    if let Some(kalan) = kaynak.split("place_id:").nth(1) {
        return format!("google:{}", kalan.trim_end_matches('/'));
    }
    match konum {
        Some((enlem, boylam)) => format!("ad:{}|{enlem:.4},{boylam:.4}", ad.to_lowercase()),
        None => format!("ad:{}", ad.to_lowercase()),
    }
}

## Dünyada bu işi yapan araçlar

| Araç | Kaynak | "Site yok" tespiti | Fiyat |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Outscraper** | Google Maps | Site alanı boş **ve** telefon + yorum + kategori şartı | İlk 500 kayıt ücretsiz, sonra $3/1.000 |
| **Apify "No-Website Leads"** | Google Maps (Places API'sini atlar) | `presence` alanı: none / social_only / booking_only / broken / has_website + 0-100 lead score | $10/1.000 eşleşen lead |
| **LeadSwift** | Maps + Yelp + Facebook + site taraması | Her alanda filtre; "claimed" durumu, bozuk site, reklam çalıştırma, HTML teknoloji araması | $24.99–$99.99/ay |
| **D7 Lead Finder** | Maps + Yelp + Facebook | Filtre yok — CSV indirip site kolonuna göre gözle ayıklıyorsun | ~$17–78/ay, 5 arama/gün ücretsiz |

**Profesyonellerin ortak standardı şu 5 madde:** (1) kaynak Google Maps — hiçbiri OSM kullanmıyor, (2) "site yok" tek başına yetmiyor; *hiç yok / sadece sosyal / ölü site* ayrımı yapılıyor, (3) telefon + yorum + aktiflik şartı aranıyor, (4) **kalıcı kayıt: durum, mükerrer engeli, kara liste**, (5) CSV dışa aktarım. # Google Places API (New) — Key Setup & 2026 Pricing

## 1. Exact console paths / URLs

Google's official setup doc is **https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/get-api-key** ("Set up the Places API (New)"). The canonical path:

| Step | Console URL |
|---|---|
| Sign in / create Cloud account | `https://console.cloud.google.com/` |
| Create project (project selector → **Create Project**) | `https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate` (project selector: `https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector2/home/dashboard`) |
| Chained setup wizard for brand-new users ("Get Started") | `https://console.cloud.google.com/getting-started` |
| Enable billing / link a billing account | `https://console.cloud.google.com/billing` |
| **Enable "Places API (New)"** | `https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/places.googleapis.com` → click **ENABLE** (shows **MANAGE** if already enabled) |
| Maps API Library (all Maps APIs) | `https://console.cloud.google.com/google/maps-apis/library` |
| **Credentials → Create credentials → API key** | `https://console.cloud.google.com/google/maps-apis/credentials` — click **Create credentials ▾ → API key** |
| Set key restrictions (API + application) | Same Credentials page → click the key name → **Edit API key** → *Key restrictions*: **API restrictions → Restrict key** (select **Places API (New)**), **Application restrictions** (IP addresses / Android / iOS / Websites) → **Save** |
| View key string later | Credentials page → **Show key** |

**gcloud equivalents** (from the same doc):
```
gcloud services enable --project "PROJECT" "places.googleapis.com"
gcloud services api-keys create --project="PROJECT_ID" --display-name="NAME" \
  --api-target=service=places.googleapis.com
```

**Key detail from the docs:** in the *Create API key* panel Google pre-selects **API restrictions** and requires at least one — you must leave **Places API (New)** selected. Also important: *"Selecting an API here doesn't enable it"* — enabling on the library page is a separate step.

### Desktop-app caveat on restrictions (important)
Google's security guidance (**https://developers.google.com/maps/api-security-best-practices**) lists exactly four application-restriction types: **Websites, IP addresses, Android apps, iOS apps**. There is **no "desktop/Windows app" restriction**. For web-service (REST) traffic Google says: *"PLATFORM_TYPE_WEBSERVICE: You may have to rely on IP address restrictions on the key, to properly restrict it."* Since a shipped desktop binary calling `places.googleapis.com` directly cannot keep a key secret, the practical options are:
- **IP restriction** (only works if your users egress via a known IP — not for consumer desktop apps), or
- **Proxy the call through your own backend** and keep the key server-side (Google's separate-keys + "split client-side and server-side usage into separate projects" guidance supports this), or
- Ship an **API-restricted-but-unrestricted-application** key and accept abuse risk. Google's explicit warning: *"An unrestricted API key can be used to make a request to any Google Maps Platform service… You are financially responsible for charges caused by abuse of unrestricted API keys."*

## 2. Is a billing account / credit card required even inside the free tier?

**Yes — unconditionally.** From the usage-and-billing page:

> *"To use the Places API, you must enable billing on each of your projects and include an API key or OAuth token with all API or SDK requests."*

And the setup page's prerequisites require *"a Google Cloud project with billing enabled."* There is no free/no-billing mode for Places API (New). The free-tier caps simply reduce the *charge* to $0; the billing account must still exist. A brand-new account can attach a **$300 / 90-day Cloud Free Trial** credit (available only if you have never been a paying GCP/Maps/Firebase customer), but it still requires a card.

## 3. Free monthly caps per SKU — Text Search (New), 2026

Effective **March 1, 2025** and current, the old $200 monthly recurring credit was **replaced** by a per-SKU free monthly usage threshold (**https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/faq**):

| SKU (billing name) | SKU code | Free/mo | 1–100k | 100k–500k | 500k–1M | 1M–5M | 5M+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Text Search Essentials (IDs Only)** | 635D-A9DD-C520 | **Unlimited (free)** | – | – | – | – | – |
| **Text Search Pro** | 4FDA-34B1-A910 | **5,000** | $32.00 | $25.60 | $19.20 | $9.60 | $2.40 |
| **Text Search Enterprise** | E967-44BC-B44D | **1,000** | $35.00 | $28.00 | $21.00 | $10.50 | $2.63 |
| **Text Search Enterprise + Atmosphere** | 120C-BEC3-B48F | **1,000** | $40.00 | $32.00 | $24.00 | $12.00 | $3.40 |

*All prices USD per 1,000 requests (global list, **https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/pricing**).* Free-cap pattern across tiers: **Essentials 10,000 / Pro 5,000 / Enterprise 1,000** per month per SKU (the 10,000 figure applies to Essentials SKUs generally, e.g. Autocomplete, Place Details Essentials, Geocoding; Text Search "Essentials" in practice only exists as the IDs-Only SKU, which is unlimited/free).

**Note on the "Essentials" row:** there is no billable "Text Search Essentials" beyond **IDs Only**, and that SKU is marked **Unlimited** free. Requesting only `places.id`, `places.name`, `places.attributions`, `nextPageToken`, etc. costs nothing.

## 4. Hard limits, field-mask billing, pagination

**Billing = highest SKU triggered by any field in the mask.** From **https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/usage-and-billing**:

> *"You are then billed at the highest SKU applicable to your request. That means if you select fields in both the Essentials and the Pro SKUs, you are billed based on the Pro SKU."*

So one `places.websiteUri` or `places.rating` (Enterprise) in the mask re-prices **the whole request** at $35/1,000, and one Atmosphere field (e.g. `places.reviews`, `places.editorialSummary`, `places.servesBeer`) re-prices it at $40/1,000 — even if the other 19 fields are Essentials.

**Field → SKU mapping for Text Search (New)** (**https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/text-search**):
- **Essentials (IDs Only):** `places.id`, `places.name`, `places.attributions`, `places.consumerAlert`, `nextPageToken`, `places.movedPlace`, `places.movedPlaceId`
- **Pro:** `places.displayName`, `places.formattedAddress`, `places.location`, `places.types`, `places.photos`, `places.primaryType`, `places.businessStatus`, `places.viewport`, `places.googleMapsUri`, etc. (note `places.displayName` — the human-readable name — is **Pro**, not Essentials)
- **Enterprise:** `places.rating`, `places.userRatingCount`, `places.websiteUri`, `places.priceLevel`, `places.priceRange`, `places.internationalPhoneNumber`, `places.nationalPhoneNumber`, `places.currentOpeningHours`, `places.regularOpeningHours`, `places.transitStation`
- **Enterprise + Atmosphere:** `places.reviews`, `places.editorialSummary`, `places.reviewSummary`, `places.generativeSummary`, `places.neighborhoodSummary`, `places.parkingOptions`, `places.paymentOptions`, `places.outdoorSeating`, `places.delivery`, `places.takeout`, `places.servesBeer`, `places.evChargeOptions`, `places.fuelOptions`, `routingSummaries`, etc.

**Field mask is mandatory** — *"There is no default list of returned fields in the response. If you omit the field mask, the method returns an error."* Wildcard `X-Goog-FieldMask: *` is discouraged in production (and bills at the highest tier).

**maxResultCount → deprecated.** `pageSize` replaces it:
> *"Specifies the number of results, between 1 and 20, to display on each page… This field replaces the deprecated maxResultCount field. If you specify both pageSize and maxResultCount, the API uses pageSize and ignores maxResultCount. If pageSize is 0 or unspecified, the API returns 20 results on each page by default. If pageSize is greater than 20, the API returns at most 20 results on each page."*

**Pagination: yes, via `pageToken`.** Response returns `nextPageToken`; send it back as `pageToken` in the next POST body. Constraint: *"All parameters other than maxResultCount, pageSize, and pageToken must be the same as the previous request. Otherwise, the API returns an INVALID_ARGUMENT error."*

**Hard cap: 60 results total across all pages.**
> *"Text Search (New) returns a maximum of 60 results across all pages, although this limit is subject to change."*

That means **max 3 pages** at the full 20/page. Each page is a separate HTTP request and thus a separate billable event — so pulling all 60 results costs **3× the per-request SKU price** (e.g. 3 × $0.032 = $0.096 at Text Search Pro list price for one query drained to 60 results).

Also note: *"The list of places returned is not guaranteed to be consistent for identical requests."* Location radius max 50,000 m; `locationBias` and `locationRestriction` are mutually exclusive; omitting both defaults to IP biasing.

## Cost bottom line for a desktop app

- **Cheapest legal config:** field mask limited to `places.id,places.displayName,places.formattedAddress,places.location` → **Text Search Pro, $32/1,000 requests, first 5,000/mo free**. Anything with rating/hours/phone/website → **$35/1,000, first 1,000/mo free**. Adding reviews → **$40/1,000, first 1,000/mo free**.
- **500 Pro-tier searches/month** → $0. **5,000/month** → $0. **10,000/month** → 5,000 free + 5,000 × $0.032 = **$160/month**.
- **IDs-Only** masks (just to enumerate Place IDs, then hydrate via Place Details) are **free and unlimited** at the Text Search step — the classic cost-reduction pattern, though you then pay Place Details SKUs (Essentials 10,000 free, Pro 5,000 free @ $17/1,000, Enterprise 1,000 free @ $20/1,000).

**Elenenler (etiket kullanımı çok düşük/sıfır):** Paintball 0 · `shop=car_glass` 2 · `shop=underwear` 1 · `shop=sportswear` 1 · `craft=machining` 3 · `amenity=comedy_club` 1 · `amenity=registry_office` 4 · `shop=hat` 29 · `shop=seeds` 13 · `shop=plant_nursery` 16 · `craft=sign_maker` 0 → bunların çoğu yakın bir gerçek etiketle eklendi (ör. paintball yerine spor tesisi), bazıları hiç eklenmedi.

## Dürüst sınır

OSM'de Türk yemek türlerinin ayrı etiketi yok: **Kebapçı/Pideci/Köfteci/Mantıcı → `amenity=restaurant`**, **Dönerci/Lahmacuncu/Çiğ Köfteci/Tavukçu → `amenity=fast_food`**. ## Yapılabilecekler

### A · Satış hunisini kapatmak (en yüksek getiri)

1. **Günlük gönderim sayacı ve 15 mesaj freni.** Bugün hiçbir sınır yok: 200 kayıt seçip arka arkaya WhatsApp açabilirsiniz — hesabın askıya alınmasının en olası sebebi bu. Defterde günlük sayaç + "bugün 15/15 doldu" uyarısı. *Küçük.*
2. **Görüşme notu ve yanıt tarihi.** Defterde serbest metin alanı ("fiyat sordu", "haftaya arayacak") + otomatik tarih; kartta ve detay panelinde görünür. *Küçük.*
3. **Takip kuyruğu ekranı.** `Takip` süzgeci var ama toplu çalışma listesi yok: "bugün aranacak 12 işletme", 3/7/14 gün kademesi, tek tuşla ikinci mesaj taslağı. *Orta.*
4. **Teklif ve ödeme takibi.** Demo beğenilince 3 paket (tek sayfa / çok sayfa / bakım), seçilen paket, tutar, ödeme durumu; kazanılan müşteri arşivi. *Orta.*
5. **Huni raporu.** Tarandı → gönderildi → yanıt → görüşme → satış oranları, haftalık özet ve CSV. *Orta.*
6. **Toplu hazırlık modu.** 10 işletme seçip mesajları sırayla hazırlama (gönderim yine elle), nerede kaldığını hatırlama. *Orta.*

### B · Mesaj ve gönderim

7. **Sektör bazında A/B.** Şu an varyant global; "kuaförde A, restoranda B" ayrı test edilemiyor. *Küçük-orta.*
8. **Örneklem uyarısı.** 30 gönderimin altında oran farkı gürültü; panelde "sonuç anlamlı değil" göstergesi. *Küçük.*
9. **WhatsApp Business Cloud API (opsiyonel).** Otomatik gönderim için tek gerçek yol; ücretsiz katman var ama işletme doğrulaması, onaylı şablon ve opt-in gerekir. *Büyük, karar gerektirir.*
10. **Göndermeden önce önizleme.** Bugün buton doğrudan tarayıcıyı açıyor; tam metin + karakter sayısı + link kontrolü gösteren bir onay adımı. *Küçük.*
11. **RET'i tek tuşla işleme.** `Reddetti` durumu zaten kara listeye alıyor; eksik olan "RET mesajı geldi" düğmesinin karttan tek tıkla erişilebilir olması. *Küçük.*

### C · Arama kalitesi

12. **Tam sınır poligonu (area) sorgusu.** Yarıçap komşu mahalleye taşıyor; `around` yerine `area` ile ilçe sınırına oturmak. *Orta.*
13. **320 sektörün verim denetimi.** Hangi sektör gerçekten sonuç döndürüyor, hangisi boş? Ölçüm olmadan "sektör çok" demek yanıltıcı. *Orta.*
14. **Google Details ile zenginleştirme.** Telefonu/saati eksik ama puanı yüksek adaylara tek çağrı; kota korumalı. *Orta.*
15. **Önbellek yönetim ekranı.** Boyut, yaş, "temizle", "önbellekten geldi" etiketi. *Küçük.*
16. **Yanlış kayıt bildirimi.** "Bu kayıt işletme değil / kapandı" işareti → kara listeye, bir daha gösterilmesin. *Küçük.*

### D · Demo ve yayın

17. **Open Graph / SEO etiketleri.** Demoda `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image` **yok** — link WhatsApp'ta bugün başlıksız, görselsiz görünüyor. Tek satırlık iş, en görünür kazanç. *Küçük.*
18. **Demo'da gerçek fotoğraf.** İşletme sahibinden gelen görseller için yükleme + galeri; şu an sektör temsili görseller var. *Orta.*
19. **Demo'ya iletişim formu / WhatsApp butonu.** Ziyaretçi tek tıkla yazabilsin; demo sahibine örnek olarak da güçlü. *Küçük.*
20. **Tema seçimi.** 2-3 renk paleti; müşteri beğenmezse tek tuşla değiştirip yeniden yayınlama. *Orta.*
21. **Yayından kaldırma.** Yalnızca yayınlama var; silinen demo GitHub'da kalıyor. *Küçük.*
22. **Eski demolara karne rozetini toplu ekleme.** Rozet bundan sonraki yayınlara giriyor. *Küçük.*
23. **Yayın geçmişi + link sağlığı.** Hangi link ne zaman üretildi, hâlâ HTTP 200 mü. *Orta.*

### E · Mühendislik

24. **Bekleyen 7 dosyayı commit + push, CI'yı yeşile doğrula.** Bugünkü işlerin hiçbiri uzakta değil. *Küçük, ilk sırada yapılmalı.*
25. **`main.rs`'i modüllere bölmek.** 10.433 satır tek dosya; arama / demo / karne / yayın / whatsapp / ui olarak ayırmak bakımı ciddi hızlandırır. *Büyük.*
26. **Ayarlar ekranı.** API anahtarı, GitHub kullanıcı-depo, günlük limit, TTL — `.env` elle düzenlemek yerine uygulama içinden. *Orta.*
27. **Arayüzde kota göstergesi.** Kalan Google araması bugün sadece dosyada/günlükte. *Küçük.*
28. **Günlüğü dosyaya yazma + hata raporu.** Panel kapanınca log kayboluyor. *Küçük.*
29. **Fixture'lı E2E test.** Kayıtlı Overpass/Google yanıtlarıyla tarama; ağ olmadan, deterministik. *Orta.*
30. **Windows exe cilası.** İkon, sürüm bilgisi, imza, otomatik güncelleme. *Orta.*

### F · Uyum ve hukuk

31. **KVKK.** Veri kaynağı, saklama süresi, silme talebi; defterde "kaydımı sil" işlemi. *Orta.*
32. **İYS / ticari ileti uyarısı.** Türkiye'de ticari elektronik ileti onay ister; ilk mesaj öncesi kontrol ve kayıt. *Orta, ama hukuki risk gerçek.*
33. **Kara liste yedeği.** Defter tek JSON dosya; bozulursa "RET" diyenler kaybolur ve tekrar mesaj gider. Otomatik yedek. *Küçük.*
34. **Repo kimliği.** README hâlâ "KARAOĞLU Zeytin Takip" diyor; Python web uygulaması da aynı repoda. İki projeyi ayırmak ya da README'yi bu projeye göre yazmak. *Küçük.*

# Dependabot: bağımlılık güncellemelerini otomatik PR olarak açar.
#
# Her PR normal "Testler" iş akışını tetikler (cargo fmt + test + clippy ve
# uçtan uca duman testi), yani kırmızı bir güncelleme birleştirilmez.
# Not: requirements.txt ve Cargo.lock sürümleri sabit tuttuğu için güncelleme
# PR'ları "elle pinleme" ihtiyacını ortadan kaldırır, yalnızca PR'ı onaylamak
# yeterlidir.
version: 2

updates:
  # Masaüstü uygulaması — Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock
  - package-ecosystem: "cargo"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: "Europe/Istanbul"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      # minor + patch tek PR'da toplanır (PR gürültüsünü azaltır);
      # major sürüm atlamaları inceleme için ayrı PR olarak gelir.
      rust-kucuk-guncellemeler:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["minor", "patch"]

  # Web sürümü — requirements.txt
  - package-ecosystem: "pip"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: "Europe/Istanbul"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      python-kucuk-guncellemeler:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["minor", "patch"]

  # İş akışlarındaki action sürümleri (checkout, setup-python, cache ...)
  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
      time: "06:00"
      timezone: "Europe/Istanbul"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      action-kucuk-guncellemeler:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["minor", "patch"]

        Ok(()) => true,
        Err(hata) => {
            logs.push(format!("[!] WhatsApp açılamadı: {hata}"));

        }

## Bu turda yapılanlar

**#5 · Ödeme takibi kuyruğa bağlandı.** Takip paneli artık iki bölüm: üstte "yanıt bekleyen", altta **ÖDEME BEKLEYEN**. Teklifi verilip 3 günü dolan ve tamamı ödenmemiş kayıtlar burada listeleniyor; her satırda paket, **kalan bakiye** ve ödeme durumu var. "Tahsilat" düğmesi kalan tutarı ve yayın linkini içeren hatırlatma mesajını hazırlıyor — günlük 15 mesaj freni burada da geçerli.

**#6 · Kısmi ödeme ayrıldı.** Yeni `tahsil_edilen` alanı: "kısmi" seçilince altında ikinci tutar alanı açılıyor, kalan bakiye anında görünüyor. Ciro artık doğru ikiye ayrılıyor — 9.000 ₺ teklifte 3.000 alındıysa `3.000 tahsil · 6.000 bekliyor`. Kalanı girince kayıt kendiliğinden "ödendi"ye geçiyor, tahsilat teklifin üstüne çıkamıyor.

**#11 · Yayından kaldırma.** Detay panelinde yayın linkinin altında **Yayından kaldır**: demo + karne `gh-pages` dalından silinir, `index.html` yenilenir, commit + push edilir; link 404 döner ve defterdeki adres temizlenir. Yayınlama kodu `yayin_dizini_yenile` / `yayin_isle` / `yayin_adresi_bul` olarak paylaşıldı, böylece iki akış aynı mantığı kullanıyor.

**#13 · Karne paylaşım etiketleri.** Karne sayfası da `og:title` (puan sınıfıyla: "… — Dijital Görünürlük Karnesi (Orta)"), `og:description`, `og:locale` ve `robots=noindex` ile üretiliyor; WhatsApp'ta başlıksız görünmüyor.

**#18 · Sektör verimi.** Sol panele **Sektör verimi** düğmesi: önbellekteki taramalara göre her sektör için "kaç ilçe tarandı · kaçında kayıt çıktı · kaç işletme", en verimli 8 sektör ve hiç kayıt döndürmeyenlerin listesi günlüğe yazılıyor.

  // Bölümler kaydırınca görünür olsun
  var gozlemci = "IntersectionObserver" in window
    ? new IntersectionObserver(function (girisler) {
        girisler.forEach(function (giris) {
          if (!giris.isIntersecting) return;
          giris.target.classList.add("in");
          gozlemci.unobserve(giris.target);
        });
      }, { threshold: 0, rootMargin: "0px 0px -8% 0px" })
    : null;
  document.querySelectorAll(".reveal").forEach(function (oge) {
    if (gozlemci) gozlemci.observe(oge); else oge.classList.add("in");
  });

  var azalt = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");

  // Kaydırmayla hareket: her katmanın kendi hızı var

    });

    if (sahne && sahneFoto) {
      var kutu = sahne.getBoundingClientRect();
      var toplam = kutu.height - window.innerHeight;
      var ilerleme = toplam > 0 ? Math.min(1, Math.max(0, -kutu.top / toplam)) : 0;
      // 1.0 → 1.22 yakınlaşma, hafif yana kayma
      sahneFoto.style.transform = "scale(" + (1 + ilerleme * 0.22).toFixed(4) + ") translate3d(" +
        (ilerleme * -3).toFixed(2) + "%," + (ilerleme * -2).toFixed(2) + "%,0)";
      if (cizgi) cizgi.style.width = (ilerleme * 100).toFixed(1) + "%";

    if (bekliyor) return;

    requestAnimationFrame(konumla);

    iste();

  var program = {
    0: [[720, 1320]],
    1: [[720, 1410]], 2: [[720, 1410]], 3: [[720, 1410]], 4: [[720, 1410]], 5: [[720, 1410]],
    6: [[720, 1320]]
  };
  var gunAdlari = ["Pazartesi", "Salı", "Çarşamba", "Perşembe", "Cuma", "Cumartesi", "Pazar"];
  function iki(s) { return String(s).padStart(2, "0"); }
  function saatMetni(d) { return iki(Math.floor(d / 60) % 24) + ":" + iki(d % 60); }
  function kalanMetni(d) {
    var gun = Math.floor(d / 1440), sa = Math.floor((d % 1440) / 60), dk = d % 60, p = [];
    if (gun > 0) p.push(gun + " gün");
    if (sa > 0) p.push(sa + " sa");
    if (dk > 0) p.push(dk + " dk");
    return p.length ? p.join(" ") : "0 dk";
  }
  function tazele() {
    var hedef = document.getElementById("acik-durum");
    if (!hedef) return;
    var simdi = new Date();
    var gun = (simdi.getDay() + 6) % 7; // Pazartesi = 0
    var dakika = simdi.getHours() * 60 + simdi.getMinutes();
    var bugun = program[gun] || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < bugun.length; i++) {
      if (dakika >= bugun[i][0] && dakika < bugun[i][1]) {
        var kalan = bugun[i][1] - dakika;
        var ayrinti = "kapanış " + saatMetni(bugun[i][1]) + " (" + kalanMetni(kalan) + " kaldı)";
        hedef.textContent = (kalan <= 15 ? "🟠 Kapanmak üzere · " : "🟢 Şu an açık · ") + ayrinti;
        hedef.style.color = kalan <= 15 ? "#fb923c" : "#4ade80";
        return;
      }
    }
    for (var j = 0; j < 7; j++) {
      var hedefGun = (gun + j) % 7;
      var dilimler = program[hedefGun] || [];
      for (var k = 0; k < dilimler.length; k++) {
        var bas = dilimler[k][0];
        if (j === 0 && bas <= dakika) continue;
        var etiket = j === 0 ? "bugün" : (j === 1 ? "yarın" : gunAdlari[hedefGun]);
        hedef.textContent = "🔴 Şu an kapalı · açılış " + etiket + " " + saatMetni(bas) +
          " · " + kalanMetni(j * 1440 + bas - dakika) + " kaldı";
        hedef.style.color = "#f87171";
        return;
      }
    }
    hedef.textContent = "";
  }
  tazele();
  setInterval(tazele, 60000);
})();

Video yaklaşımını bıraktım; sayfa artık **gerçek fotoğraflarla** çalışıyor ve üç yerde farklı şekilde hareket ediyor.

## 1. Açılış — fotoğraf bizden yavaş kayar

Fotoğraf, yazıdan yavaş hareket eder (derinlik hissi). Ölçtüm: sayfa en üstte `translateY(-21.6px)`, 420px kaydırınca `+70.3px` — yani içerik yukarı çıkarken fotoğraf geriden geliyor.

![Açılış — fotoğraf paralaks](screenshots/fotolu-final-hero.png)

## 2. Sabit sahne — kaydırdıkça fotoğraf yakınlaşır ve kayar

Bu bölümde fotoğraf ekranda **sabit kalır**, siz kaydırdıkça büyür ve yana kayar. İlerleme çubuğu da doluyor:

| Kaydırma | Ölçek | Yana kayma | Çubuk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Başlangıç | 1.00 | 0% | %0 |
| Orta | **1.08** | −1.1% | %36.7 |
| Son | **1.22** | −3.0% | %100 |

![Sabit sahne — ortada](screenshots/fotolu-sahne-a.png)

![Sabit sahne — sonunda](screenshots/fotolu-sahne-b.png)

## 3. Galeri — iki sütun farklı hızda

Her fotoğrafın kendi hızı var (`0.16 / 0.05 / 0.24 / 0.10`), aynı anda ölçtüğüm kaymalar: **30.6 / 1.5 / 37.4 / −9 px**. Böylece sütunlar birbirinden bağımsız akıyor.

![Galeri — kademeli paralaks](screenshots/fotolu-galeri.png)

Mobilde de taşma yok, alt sabit arama düğmesi yerinde:

![Mobil](screenshots/fotolu-mobil.png)

## Fotoğraflar nereden

Wikimedia Commons'tan 4 gerçek restoran fotoğrafı (CC BY-SA 4.0, fotoğrafçı **Basile Morin**). Lisans gereği sayfa altbilgisine atıf yazdım, kaynak listesi `demos/medya/foto/kaynak.json` içinde. Deneme için stok görsel; **gerçek işletme fotoğraflarıyla değiştirilecek**.

Boyut için **WebP**'ye çevirdim: 1.9 MB → **648 KB** (4 fotoğraf). Hepsi `200` dönüyor, konsolda hata yok.

## Test ederken bulup düzelttiğim iki hata

1. **Fotoğraf kayarken kart içinde boşluk kalıyordu** — fotoğrafı %20 taşkın yapıp kaymayı kart yüksekliğinin ±%8.5'iyle sınırladım; artık kenarda boşluk görünmüyor.
2. **Mobilde açılış içeriği kesiliyordu** — `92vh` + `overflow-hidden` metni kırpıyordu (ölçtüm: içerik 776px'lik bölüme sığmıyordu). `min-h-[92vh]`'a çevirdim, "Kaydırın ↓" satırı artık görünüyor.

Ayrıca `prefers-reduced-motion` açıksa hiçbir transform uygulanmıyor, JS kapalıysa bölümler normal akışta duruyor.

## Sınırlar

- **Uygulamaya bağlanmadı:** sayfa elle kuruldu, `demos/` klasörü `.gitignore`'da — yani ne depoda ne yayında. "Demo Üret & Gönder" hâlâ eski şablonu üretiyor.
- Metinler **yer tutucu** ("Salonun hikâyesi", kapasite 84 kişi gibi) — işletmeden gelen gerçek bilgi değil.
- Fotoğraflar **stok**; işletmenin kendi fotoğrafları olmadan bu görünüm gerçek müşteriye gönderilmemeli (CC atıfı da taşımak zorunda kalırsınız).
- Tailwind CDN bağımlılığı sürüyor.

## 3. "1000 free HTML templates zip" tarzı toplu paketler — yasal mı?

**Kısa cevap: Çoğunlukla HAYIR / yüksek riskli; en azından "kanıtlanmış temiz" sayılmaz.**

Kendi testimle gördüklerim:

1. **"1600+ free templates" gibi başlıklar aslında aynı sitenin ücretsiz kataloğudur**, tek bir ZIP değil. ThemeWagon'un kendi "bundle" ürünü bile pazarlama sırasında **1.06 GB ZIP** olarak veriliyor ve *lisansı yine tema bazında değişiyor* — bazı temalarda footer kredisi zorunlu (https://themewagon.com/themes/template-collection-2022-one-hundred-free-html5-templates-in-one-bundle/ → "License" bölümü ve "Open source · Use in commercial projects" ibaresi; ama ThemeWagon'un genel lisansı "yazarın atıf kuralına bakın" diyor). Yani **"100 bundle" paketi ≠ "100'ü de sınırsız kullan"**.
2. **GitHub'daki "170/1000 templates" repoları genelde yeniden dağıtım.** Örnek: `https://github.com/dawidolko/Website-Templates` — 170 HTML5/Bootstrap şablonu; README'de "Free to edit… Nothing here needs a build step or **or a licence key**" diyor ama **her şablonun orijinal lisansı (TemplateMonster/ThemeWagon/BootstrapMade vb.) belirtilmemiş.** Şablon adları (`moto-business-html5`, `aroma-beauty-and-spa`, `beauty-salon-bootstrap`, `car-care-auto-mobile`, `touch-hospital-medical`) doğrudan ticari pazar yerlerinin dosya adlarıyla aynı → büyük olasılıkla **kopya/toplu indirme**. MIT/CC0 olduğu kanıtlanmadıkça ticari işte kullanmak **telif ihlali riski** taşır.
3. **Aynı içerik farklı isimlerle tekrar dolaşıyor** ("1000 free HTML templates", "5000 templates zip", "mega pack"). Bu paketlerde tipik sorunlar:
   - Lisans dosyası yok / README'de sadece "free to use" yazıyor — **yasal bir lisans beyanı değil**.
   - İçinde **premium şablonlar** var (TemplateMonster, Envato Elements, BootstrapMade Pro) → yeniden dağıtımı lisansla **yasak**.
   - Eski Bootstrap 3/jQuery sürümleri, kırık CDN linkleri, büyük "demo" resimleri → **kötü kalite**.
   - Bazı paketlerde `<?php` shell/backdoor, spam SEO linkleri.
4. **Ne zaman yasal olur?** Yalnızca paketin içindeki her şablonun **MIT / CC0 / CC BY / public domain** lisansı **ayrı ayrı belgelenmişse** ve sen **CC BY atıflarını koruyorsan**. Aksi halde "toplu zip" değil, **orijinal kaynaktan tek tek indirin**.

**Altın kural:** Bir şablonun kullanım hakkı, onu **ilk yayınlayan** sitede yazan lisansla belirlenir (ThemeWagon'un kendi lisansı bile "orijinal yazarın lisansına bakın" diyor). Toplu paket bu zinciri koparır.

1. **Start Bootstrap** (MIT, Bootstrap 5, sektör bazlı hazır tema) — *en güvenli.*

6. **ThemeWagon** — sektör etiketleri çok iyi (Feane restoran, Clinic, Garo Estate), **ama tema sayfasındaki atıf notunu mutlaka okuyun**.

Bu klasör, demo üretirken **tasarım referansı** olarak kullanılan, lisansı temiz
şablonları tutar. Buradaki dosyalar doğrudan kopyalanıp müşteriye satılmaz;
bölüm sırası, boşluk ölçeği, tipografi ve bileşen fikri alınır — HTML kendi
üreticimizde yeniden yazılır.

## Neden bu kaynaklar

Videodaki ("cinematic website") tarzın çalışan, ücretsiz karşılığı şu üç kaynaktan
geliyor. Hepsi **MIT** lisanslı: ticari kullanım serbest, atıf zorunlu değil.

| Klasör | Kaynak | Lisans | Ne için |
|---|---|---|---|
| `startbootstrap-creative/` | https://github.com/StartBootstrap/startbootstrap-creative | MIT | Diş kliniği, kuaför, düğün — büyük başlık + galeri + iletişim |
| `startbootstrap-one-page-wonder/` | https://github.com/StartBootstrap/startbootstrap-one-page-wonder | MIT | Oto servis, çekici, emlak — sıralı bölüm akışı |
| `tailwind-toolbox-landing/` | https://github.com/tailwindtoolbox/Landing-Page | MIT (kod) | Restoran, kafe, herhangi bir landing — Tailwind grid |

## Kullanım kuralları (önemli)

1. **Kopyala-yapıştır satış yok.** Şablonlar tasarım referansı; çıktımız tek
   dosyalık, kendi ürettiğimiz HTML.
2. **Demo görselleri kopyalanmaz.** Start Bootstrap şablonlarındaki `assets/`
   klasörünü bilerek almadık; Tailwind Toolbox'ın `hero.png` dosyası Freepik
   kaynaklı ve atıf istiyor — o yüzden o da alınmadı. Fotoğraflarımız kendi
   kaynağımızdan gelir.
3. **Lisans dosyaları silinmez.** Her klasördeki `LICENSE` olduğu gibi durur.
4. **Yasak kaynaklar** (araştırmayla doğrulandı):
   - **BootstrapMade ücretsiz** — "Designed by BootstrapMade" footer kredisi
     zorunlu ve *"müşteri işi için kullanamazsınız"* maddesi var.
   - **"1000 free HTML templates.zip" türü toplu paketler** — lisans zinciri
     kopuk, içinde ücretli şablonlar ve eski/kırık dosyalar var. Kullanmayın.
   - **ThemeWagon** — atıf kuralı tema bazında değişiyor; kullanılacaksa her
     temanın kendi notunu okuyun.
5. **HTML5 UP** tasarımları çok iyi ama **CC BY 3.0**: footer'da atıf zorunlu.
   Müşteri işinde atıf istemiyorsak kullanmayız.

| Sektör | Referans | Alınan fikir |
|---|---|---|
| Restoran, kafe, meyhane | `tailwind-toolbox-landing` | Menü ızgarası, iki sütun hero, "örnek menü" notu |
